issues.legal_issue: A contractual promise to permit development at a level requiring governmental approval does not create an enforceable right when that approval has not authorized the promised development.
material_facts: The development authority offered a commercial plot on the stated basis that the maximum floor space index would be 2, and the lease agreement repeated that limit.
Before the lease was executed, the State Government sanctioned a floor space index of 1.50 for the relevant use, rather than the proposed limit of 2.
The authority declined to approve the lessee’s building plan because it exceeded the approved limit.
issues.conclusion: The contractual term providing for a floor space index of 2 did not bestow a legally enforceable right because the required governmental sanction had not authorized that limit.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 21 and 22(m) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, development controls including the percentage of building area for a plot form part of the development plan. Sections 31(6) and 37(1)–(2) make the sanctioned final plan and sanctioned modifications binding; section 159 concerns regulations made with prior State Government approval. The FSI is defined by regulation 3.11 and its maximum is prescribed by regulation 16.3.1. A contractual term cannot confer a legal right to development that the required governmental approval has not authorized. No earlier case is cited for this issue.

predicates.writ_mandamus_claim: A person sought a writ requiring a public development authority to permit a proposed development.
predicates.development_right_requires_government_ap: The proposed development right depended on governmental approval of the applicable development controls.
predicates.approval_did_not_authorize_promised_deve: The government approved a development limit lower than the limit promised in the parties’ agreement.

issues.definition: When a person seeks a writ to enforce a promised development right that depends on governmental approval, the promise creates no enforceable right if the approval did not authorize that development.

issues.legal_issue: A development authority may prescribe floor space index limits through development controls, but those limits acquire legal effect through the required governmental approval and form part of the development plan.
material_facts: The Act required a development plan to provide for control of land use and development, including the percentage of building area for a plot.
The development authority adopted regulations defining FSI and prescribing maximum permissible limits, with the State Government’s prior approval for the regulations.
The authority proposed increasing the FSI for commercial use to 2, but the State Government sanctioned an increase only to 1.50.
issues.conclusion: The FSI could be fixed through regulations as part of the development plan; the proposed increase to 2 could not take effect without the required governmental sanction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22(m) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 requires development plans to provide for controls on development, including the percentage of building area for a plot. Sections 21 and 31 govern preparation and sanction of the plan, while section 31(6) makes the sanctioned plan binding on the planning authority. Section 37(1)–(2) governs minor modifications and requires State Government sanction; section 159 empowers the making of regulations with prior State Government approval. Regulations 3.11 and 16.3.1 define FSI and prescribe its maximum. The FSI limit is not merely an internal policy that the authority may disregard in a contract. No earlier case is cited for this issue.

predicates.development_plan_requires_building_area_: The governing planning scheme requires the development plan to control building area on plots.
predicates.authority_prescribes_floor_space_limits: A development authority uses development controls to set limits on the floor area permitted on a plot.
predicates.required_governmental_approval_governs_t: The legal effect of the controls or a proposed change to them depends on governmental approval.

issues.definition: Where a planning scheme requires building-area controls, an authority may prescribe floor space limits through development controls, but a change requiring governmental approval is not effective until approved.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory estoppel cannot require a public authority to perform a promise that is contrary to law or beyond its lawful authority.
material_facts: The authority’s lease agreement stated that the lessee could develop at an FSI of 2.
The State Government had sanctioned a lower FSI for the relevant use, and the authority refused to approve a plan relying on the higher contractual figure.
The lessee invoked estoppel to require the authority to honor the contractual representation.
issues.conclusion: The lessee could not invoke promissory estoppel to compel the authority to honor a contractual term that conflicted with the sanctioned development controls.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 concerns estoppel. The Court applied the settled principle that promissory estoppel cannot compel a public body or the Government to carry out a representation or promise that is contrary to law or outside its authority or power. Sections 31(6) and 37(2) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 make the sanctioned development plan and sanctioned modifications binding; section 159 concerns the authority to make regulations. No earlier case is cited in the judgment for this principle.

predicates.writ_mandamus_claim: A person sought a writ requiring a public authority to perform a promise.
predicates.public_authority_made_a_promise: A public authority represented that a person could proceed on a stated basis.
predicates.promise_conflicts_with_binding_law_or_ex: The promised action conflicted with binding legal controls or was beyond the authority’s lawful power.

issues.definition: In a claim seeking to compel a public authority to perform its promise, estoppel cannot require performance when the promise conflicts with binding law or exceeds the authority’s lawful power.

issues.legal_issue: A writ of mandamus is unavailable unless the applicant establishes a legally protected and judicially enforceable right.
material_facts: The lessee sought a writ compelling the authority and the State Government to withdraw the notification and the refusal to approve the building plan.
The contractual FSI limit had not been authorized by the required governmental sanction, so it did not confer a legally enforceable right.
The High Court dismissed the writ petition, and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The requested relief was unavailable because the lessee had not established a legally protected and judicially enforceable right.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that a person seeking a writ of mandamus must prove a legally protected and judicially enforceable right. The statutory setting included sections 31(6) and 37(2) of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, under which the sanctioned development plan and sanctioned modifications bind the planning authority. No earlier case is cited for the mandamus principle.

predicates.writ_mandamus_claim: An applicant asks a court to issue a writ compelling a public authority to act.
predicates.applicant_lacks_legally_protected_enforc: The applicant has no legally protected right that a court can enforce.

issues.definition: A court cannot grant mandamus when the applicant seeks that writ but lacks a legally protected and judicially enforceable right.
